# 06 — Scale bars on annotator crops

**State: CLOSED — landed, wired, and on by default in the HDF5/Hub export.**
Updated 2026-11-13 after rebasing onto GitLab `main`: the wiring Veit referred
to does exist, and an earlier revision of this file wrongly called it missing.

## Why it is built the way it is
Crops shown to annotators need a size reference, but crops are also
**classifier input**. A bar burnt into the image is an appearance change the
ViT never saw in training — the same class of mismatch that cost 83-93% of the
living rate when the deconvolution changed. So the bar must be **exactly
removable**, and it must never reach a model.

The pre-existing `utils.add_scale_bar` could not be undone: it padded **left
and right** for narrow crops, and centred padding is unrecoverable from pixels.

## Where it lives now: `scale_bar.py`
Added in `7492061` inside `utils.py`, then **lifted into its own module**
(`6cb4b48`) so callers needing only a bar do not pay for `utils`' imports —
that module pulls in torch, transformers, pandas and matplotlib at module
scope, none of which are installed on the processing workers. `scale_bar.py`
needs nothing but Pillow. `utils` re-exports the names, so old callers still
work.

* `add_scale_bar_strip(img, pixel_resolution=PIXEL_SIZE_UM)` — appends a fixed
  **34-row strip below**; never alters the crop's own pixels.
* Bar is **1 mm where it fits, else 500 um**, with no shorter step. A crop too
  narrow for a 500 um bar is **padded on the right**, so the object stays
  left-aligned in the same place every time.
* `save_crop_with_scale_bar()` records the original size in a **PNG text
  chunk**; `strip_scale_bar()` restores it exactly (strip **and** padding).
* Verified byte-identical round trips from 10 px wide (padded to 28) to 1951 px.

The 500 um floor came from real data: on an SO308 sample **19% of living and
87% of not-living** crops were too narrow — the earlier adaptive ladder gave
those useless 20-50 um bars.

### Pixel size was corrected to 22.5 um/px (`ad1b926`)
`PIXEL_SIZE_UM = 4.5 * (400/160) * 2` — PISCO2 optics at 2560x2560: a 4.5 um
sensor pixel, 400/160 inverse magnification, binning 2. It was **23** until
2026-09-09, which disagreed with `area_to_esd()` by **2.2%**. Defined once and
imported by the exporter, so a **drawn bar and a reported `object_esd` now
agree**. Anything measured off a bar drawn before that date is 2.2% out.

## How it is wired
`export_hdf5_to_ecotaxa.py` imports `PIXEL_SIZE_UM`, `SCALE_BAR_STRIP_H` and
`save_crop_with_scale_bar`, and exposes:

* `--scale-bar / --no-scale-bar` (`BooleanOptionalAction`, **default on**)
* `--pixel-size` (default `PIXEL_SIZE_UM`), used for the bar **and** `object_esd`

Both are surfaced as Hub parameters in `toolbox.json` under
`pisco_ecotaxa_export`.

## Why no `strip_scale_bar()` is needed in the ViT path
This was listed as an open item; it is not one. In the current architecture
**no model ever sees a barred crop**:

* `vit_classify_hdf5.iter_crops()` reads crops straight from the segmenter's
  `result.h5`. The bar is drawn only at **export** time, after classification.
* `training/build_trainset.py` imports that **same `iter_crops`** — literally
  the inference function — or falls back to the old pipeline's
  `deconv_crops*.zip`. `training/README.md` states the rule explicitly: *"The
  EcoTaxa export zips are not a source: their PNGs carry a scale bar no model
  was trained with."*
* `train_vit.py` asserts at startup that its preprocessing equals
  `vit_classify_hdf5.preprocess` and exits if it has drifted.

So the bar is confined to the annotator-facing export. Keep it that way: the
moment anyone trains from an export zip, this guarantee is gone.

## Caveat that remains
Undoing the **padding** depends on the PNG text chunk surviving. Read crops
with PIL, which preserves it. If they come back through something that
re-encodes and drops metadata, only the bottom strip can be removed — right
padding is indistinguishable from genuine white background. The alternative,
if that ever matters, is padding *every* crop to a fixed minimum width so the
geometry is uniform and inferable without metadata.

## Loose ends in the OLD python route
The old `process_pisco_profiles.py` route never got the reversible bar:

* all four `create_ecotaxa_zips` call sites still pass
  `add_scale_bar_to_deconv=False`;
* `create_ecotaxa_zips` still calls the **old, non-reversible** `add_scale_bar`
  and still defaults to **`pixel_resolution=23`**, the superseded figure —
  while `add_scale_bar` itself now defaults to `PIXEL_SIZE_UM`. If that path is
  ever switched on, it will draw 2.2%-wrong bars.
* Project **23286**'s bars were applied by post-processing the zips by hand,
  before the wiring existed.

Only worth fixing if the old route is still to be used; otherwise the HDF5
route supersedes it.

> real export / leave the old route alone>.
EOF

# 09 — PIScO Hub integration, and what it changes for us

**State: landed on both repos' GitLab `main`.** `process_pisco_profiles` is
now **reconciled** (this session's work rebased on top, 2026-11-13).
`pisco_segmenter` local is still **9 commits behind** and was reviewed
read-only — nothing pulled or merged.

Read this first: it reframes where the other topics' code lives. Everything in
topics 01-07 was done on the **old python route**; the Hub work adds a
**second, now-primary route** through the C++ segmenter's `result.h5`.

## The two routes

| | old python route | HDF5 / Hub route |
|---|---|---|
| driver | `process_pisco_profiles.py`, `orchestrate_gpus.py` | Hub tasks in `toolbox.json`, `run*.sh` |
| crops | `Crops/`, `Deconv_crops/` + per-profile TSV | inside **`result.h5`** |
| export | `utils.create_ecotaxa_zips`, `export_ecotaxa_zips.py` | **`export_hdf5_to_ecotaxa.py`** |
| classify | in-pipeline dual ViT | **`vit_classify_hdf5.py`** |
| scale bar | not wired, old non-reversible fn | **on by default**, reversible (topic 06) |

Both still exist; the old route is what produced every number in this session.

## What landed on `process_pisco_profiles` (31 commits, 2026-09-09 .. 10-21)

A **closed retraining loop**, each step a Hub task with a `run_*.sh` wrapper:

```
segmenter result.h5
  → pisco_vit_classify     (vit_classify_hdf5.py; fp16 on tensor-core GPUs,
                            loader workers; chainable so stage 2 only sees
                            stage 1's living calls)
  → pisco_ecotaxa_export   (export_hdf5_to_ecotaxa.py; PNGs straight into the
                            zip from a process pool, predictions carried in
                            the TSV, scale bar, object_esd, sample_ctd_cast,
                            object_frame_index, link back to raw data)
  → pisco_ecotaxa_import   (ecotaxa_import.py; creates or adds to a project,
                            single pass since predictions ride along)
  → pisco_ecotaxa_features (ecotaxa_write_features.py; ViT CLS embeddings into
                            EcoTaxa so "similar to" works — the tool used
                            heavily during the not-living re-screening, topic 03)
  →  … humans annotate …
  → pisco_ecotaxa_labels   (ecotaxa_fetch_labels.py)
  → pisco_vit_trainset     (training/build_trainset.py)
  → pisco_vit_train        (training/train_vit.py, run once per stage)
  → back to pisco_vit_classify
```

Supporting pieces: `scale_bar.py` (topic 06), `crops.py` (`tight_masked`),
`ecotaxa_taxonomy_map.{py,json}` translating ViT labels to EcoTaxa taxon ids
— including the ATAIIR2604 multiclass labels — `ecotaxa_mirror.py` to copy
projects between EcoTaxa instances, and `ecotaxa_grant_annotators.py`.

Two details worth carrying:
* **Objects land as Biota**, with numeric EcoTaxa taxon ids written from the
  taxonomy map. The deprecated-taxon remap of topic 03 is the same problem this
  map now solves properly.
* `.gitignore` now excludes the **local** credentials file; only
  `process_pisco_profiles.config.example.json` is versioned (see topic 08).

## What landed on `pisco_segmenter` (9 commits, not pulled)
`88c8015` headless GPU worker · `0b8b3be` describe pipeline as a Hub tool ·
`87cd167`+`87df281` write `result.h5` alongside PNG/CSV · `acab6ed` make the
circular FOV mask switchable · `9f5fe67` **estimate the background as the C++
segmenter does** · `d15dcea` merge · `4af9b4d` **correct the background per
block** · `8eff671` read frames from a profile dataset as well as a directory.

**All four of this session's segmenter commits survive intact** on that branch
(`99a0d88`, `c1e03cd`, `8480520` crop isolation, `b805b9a` hang fix) — verified
by ancestry and by grepping the merged files.

## Does it change our workflow? **Yes — materially.**

### Background estimation changed, and there is no switch
| | before (what every result in this session used) | after |
|---|---|---|
| scope | per-frame **rolling window**, frame excluded | **per block of 12**, one background shared by the block |
| estimator | `np.max(bg_imgs)` | **max over pairwise minima** |

`PISCO_BG_SIZE` overrides the block size (default **12**); the *estimator*
itself has no legacy path.

**Why it was done** is sound and worth knowing: 12 is the stack the LUCYD
background textures were built with, so this keeps the **deconvolution input in
distribution**. That is a real improvement to the deconvolution step.

**But it changes the cleaned frame**, therefore the deconvolved crop,
therefore the thresholded contours. So:
1. **Object counts and crop appearance will differ** from everything recorded
   in this session. Abundances are not comparable across the change.
2. It is a **fourth domain shift** stacked on deconvolution model, crop
   isolation and classifier. Both published ViTs (`Veit/M181_*`,
   `Veit/ATAIIR2604_NorthSea_*`) were trained on **old-background** crops.
3. The gain is real but **unmeasured for classification** — better LUCYD input
   does not automatically mean better crops for a classifier trained on the old
   look. Treat it the way the deconvolution comparison was treated: measure,
   do not assume.

### Smaller changes
* **Input**: `frames.py` reads a directory **or** a `profile_dataset.h5`.
  Directory input still works, so existing invocations are unaffected.
* **Output**: `result.h5` is written **alongside** the PNGs and CSVs, not
  instead of them. Note its mask is **the object's own contour**, unlike the
  PNG crops, which are cut with the **accumulated frame mask** — independent
  confirmation of the accumulation behaviour found during the isolation work
  (topic 02). The HDF5 route's `--isolate` reproduces isolation from that mask.
* **FOV mask** is now overridable (`mask_img_override`); the default is
  unchanged (on).
* New knobs: `PISCO_BG_SIZE` (12), `PISCO_DECONV_BATCH`, `PISCO_LOG_FILE`.
* `run_profile.py` + `toolbox.json` package the segmenter as a Hub tool — a
  second entry point beside `orchestrate_gpus.py`.

## Decisions this forces
1. **Pull the segmenter or stay pinned?** Pulling silently changes the output
   of every future run. If SO308 is to stay comparable with the Madagascar
   subset already processed, either finish SO308 on the current code or re-run
   the two completed profiles after pulling.
2. **If standardising on the block background**, both ViTs want retraining on
   matching crops — and that is also the moment to settle the deconvolution
   choice (topic 02) and switch crop isolation on, so one retrain absorbs all
   three shifts instead of three retrains. The Hub loop above now makes that a
   chain of tasks rather than hand-run scripts.
3. **GitHub mirror of the segmenter is behind** and has not received these
   commits (topic 08).

## New-chat prompt
> Read docs/handoff/09-hub-integration.md. The segmenter's background
> estimation changed to per-block max-of-pairwise-minima and the HDF5/Hub route
> is now primary. I want to <measure the background change's effect on
> crops/classification before pulling / pull and retrain the ViTs through the
> Hub task chain / keep SO308 pinned to the current code>.
EOF
wc -l 09-hub-integration.md

Since 2026-09 (31 commits by Veit, GitLab `main`) `process_pisco_profiles` has **two parallel routes**. Check which one you are working on before editing — the old file paths still exist and still work.

| | old python route | HDF5 / Hub route (primary) |
|---|---|---|
| driver | `process_pisco_profiles.py`, `orchestrate_gpus.py` | Hub tasks in `toolbox.json`, `run*.sh` |
| crops | `Crops/`, `Deconv_crops/` + per-profile TSV | inside the C++ segmenter's **`result.h5`** |
| export | `utils.create_ecotaxa_zips`, `export_ecotaxa_zips.py` | **`export_hdf5_to_ecotaxa.py`** |
| classify | in-pipeline dual ViT | **`vit_classify_hdf5.py`** |

## What the GitLab reconciliation turned up

The rejected push wasn't a problem, it was the answer to three of your open questions. GitLab had **31 commits** of yours on top of my base — and crucially, they build *on* my work rather than conflicting with it. Rebase was clean.

**Your "I have wired them in at another point" — found it.** The scale bars are wired, and my doc was wrong to call them missing:
- You lifted the helpers out of `utils.py` into [scale_bar.py](scale_bar.py) — good call, since `utils` imports torch/transformers/pandas/matplotlib at module scope and the processing workers have none of those.
- Wired into [export_hdf5_to_ecotaxa.py](export_hdf5_to_ecotaxa.py) with `--scale-bar` **default on**, surfaced as a Hub parameter.
- You corrected the pixel size to **22.5 µm/px** (`ad1b926`) — I had 23, which disagrees with `area_to_esd()` by 2.2%.

**The "strip_scale_bar in the ViT path" item I flagged is moot** — and your architecture is why. Classification reads `result.h5` via `iter_crops`, training imports *that same function*, and `train_vit.py` asserts its preprocessing equals `vit_classify_hdf5.preprocess` at startup. No model can see a barred crop. `training/README.md` states the rule outright.

## Docs fixed to the current layout

Rewrote **06** (inverted conclusion) and **09** (now covers both repos + the closed retrain loop `classify → export → import → features → labels → trainset → train`), patched **04** (recipe rewritten upstream), **08** (per-repo remote state), and the **README** with a two-routes preamble — since topics 01–07 all describe the old route, and their data findings carry over but their file paths may not.

Two real loose ends I recorded rather than touched: `create_ecotaxa_zips` still defaults to `pixel_resolution=23` and still calls the non-reversible `add_scale_bar`, so the old route would draw 2.2%-wrong bars if switched on. And project **23286**'s bars were hand-applied before the fix, so they carry that error.

## One thing needs your call

**GitLab: pushed** (`b07f629..65df4a8`). **GitHub: not pushed.** It sits at `cbc2377` — my pre-rebase docs commit from earlier today — which the rebase replaced, so the push is a non-fast-forward. I checked: that commit is the *only* thing GitHub has that the new history doesn't, and it's mine, not yours. A `--force-with-lease=main:cbc2377` would sync it safely, but the sandbox blocked it as a destructive git action.

Run this when you're ready, or tell me to and approve the prompt:

git push --force-with-lease=main:cbc2377 git@github.com:vdausmann/process_pisco_profiles.git main

Branch is up:

```
gitlab/pre-hub-background -> b805b9a
```

Verified it contains all four of this session's segmenter commits (`99a0d88`, `c1e03cd`, `8480520` crop isolation, `b805b9a` hang fix) and that it's byte-identical to your current working tree — empty diff against local `HEAD`. Since it points at a commit `main` already had, it added no content and can be deleted any time with no consequence.

Recorded it in [09-hub-integration.md](docs/handoff/09-hub-integration.md) and [08-infrastructure.md](docs/handoff/08-infrastructure.md), pushed to GitLab as `f86b3ff`, and added it to memory so future sessions don't have to rediscover it.

## One gap the branch doesn't close

The pin makes "stay on the old background" reproducible, but it **doesn't make it automatic**. Your local checkout is still on `main` at `b805b9a` — so a plain `git pull` in that repo still jumps you forward 9 commits and silently changes the background estimator mid-campaign. The branch only helps if something is actually sitting on it.

If you want that risk gone, this switches the checkout and changes **zero files** (same commit, so it's safe even with runs in flight):

```
cd /home/veit/PIScO_dev/pisco_segmenter
git checkout -b pre-hub-background --track gitlab/pre-hub-background
```

After that, `git pull` keeps you pinned, and moving to the Hub code becomes a deliberate `git checkout main`. I left it alone in case tooling or scripts of yours assume the repo is on `main` — say the word and I'll switch it.

Worth noting the GitHub mirror (`origin`) doesn't have the new branch either; same credential situation as before, so it'd need the SSH URL.
